methodological_rigor.justification: The design is a nationwide population-based cohort of 778,943 Swedish women with linkage across SVEVAC, NVR, PDR, NPR, NCR and related registries, with HPV vaccination treated as a time-varying exposure, delayed entry, and attained age as the underlying time scale, all appropriate choices that minimize immortal-time bias. Poisson regression with age-adjusted and fully adjusted models, 1- and 2-year buffer-period sensitivity analyses, and anatomic-site-stratified analyses strengthen rigor. Confounders include calendar year, county, mother's birth country, parental education, income, and parental HPV-related disease history; however, smoking and sexual activity are acknowledged as unmeasured, and no formal power calculation is reported (sample size clearly adequate). Differential outcome ascertainment by vaccination status (screening attendance) is acknowledged but not quantitatively addressed via a negative control or bias analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual population-based cohort study using linked national registries, which maps to Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question (whether quadrivalent HPV vaccination reduces high-grade vulvovaginal lesions) directly informs vaccination policy, especially the age-at-vaccination and program-type comparisons relevant to catch-up and school-based programs. Endpoints are registry-defined precancers plus cancers (clinically meaningful surrogates for invasive disease), and the magnitude of effect (fully adjusted IRR 0.45 for ages 10-16) supports expanded early vaccination. Findings replicate and extend a single prior Danish observational study, reinforcing generalizability in Nordic registry settings.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the correct standard for this observational cohort and the authors explicitly state adherence. Key items are well addressed: eligibility criteria, exposure/outcome definitions with ICD-10 codes, time-varying exposure handling, covariate handling (including an explicit 'missing' category), sensitivity analyses, and a flow diagram (Figure 1). Minor omissions include absence of a formal risk-of-bias/sensitivity on differential screening attendance beyond narrative. Data and code availability are not described in the available text; Swedish registry data have known access restrictions through ethics permissions, but no code repository, analysis script, or data access procedure is cited.

novelty_literature.justification: The empirical finding (quadrivalent HPV vaccine reduces high-grade vulvovaginal lesions, with greater effect at younger ages) replicates a 2021 Danish registry study (Dehlendorff et al.) and extends systematic review findings from phase II/III trials. Novelty is incremental: a second Nordic registry replication with similar design, plus the addition of birth-cohort-level comparisons across opportunistic vs. subsidized vs. catch-up programs, which is a modest methodological/population extension. The authors appropriately position the work relative to the Danish cohort and the trial-based review without over-claiming firsts.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well organized with a conventional STROBE-aligned structure; abstract is self-contained and quantitatively grounded with IRRs, CIs, and follow-up durations. Methods are detailed and the time-varying exposure logic is explained with a worked example in the Figure 2 caption. The Discussion appropriately contextualizes against the Danish study and acknowledges residual confounding, misclassification, and ascertainment limitations. Minor: duplicative abstract-style sentences in the opening block and some repetition between the Discussion and Strengths/Limitations sections.

key_strengths: Very large nationwide registry cohort (n=778,943) with long follow-up and comprehensive multi-registry linkage
Appropriate time-varying exposure, delayed-entry, attained-age time scale, reducing immortal-time bias
Robust sensitivity analyses with 1- and 2-year buffer periods and site-stratified (vulvar vs vaginal) analyses
Policy-relevant comparison across opportunistic, subsidized, and catch-up birth-cohort programs showing dose-response-like population impact
Clear STROBE-aligned reporting with explicit acknowledgment of key limitations
key_concerns: Residual confounding by smoking and sexual activity, which are unmeasured in registries and only partially proxied by parental SES
Differential outcome ascertainment via screening attendance acknowledged but not quantitatively addressed (e.g., negative control, bias analysis)
Empirical novelty is incremental: largely replicates a prior Danish registry study with similar design and effect direction
No data or code availability statement visible; registry access path not described for reproducibility
Vulvovaginal cancer not analyzable separately due to few cases, limiting the hardest clinical endpoint
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, policy-relevant Nordic registry cohort that replicates and modestly extends prior work; sits comfortably in tier 2 (e.g., journals in the 10-19 JIF range) with minor revisions to strengthen bias quantification and reproducibility reporting, but lacks the novelty required for tier 1.
